articleTitle: Floating Solar Photovoltaic System: An Overview and their Feasibility at Kaptai in Rangamati
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Nowadays solar power is a remarkable sector of renewable energy. It is used for various things such as commercial application, solar heaters, solar pumps, etc. Solar power minimizes the scarcity of the integrated grid power. In the future, the power demand of our country will be increasing day by day. However, it decreases the reliability of conventional fuel. To implement solar photovoltaic (PV) power plant, it needed vast amount of land which is very difficult to an overcrowded province like Bangladesh. On the contrary, Bangladesh has a huge coastal area, lake, pond, reservoir on water to implement the solar project instead of land. 57 Major rivers and huge coastal area will be effective for implementing floating solar PV power plant. Floating PV is not only innovative access but also conventional approach of using PV modules in water framework to preserve the land as well as module increases the efficiency. Also, Floating PV infrastructure contributes to reducing the water evaporation from the water body. Kaptai, Rangamati is the best places to construct a floating solar PV power plant. FPV power project in kaptai is adept by estimating quantity like panel position, efficiency of solar panel, available surface area, economic and environmental benefits which shows the comprehensive model of total electricity production in kaptai floating PV power plant. The electrical production of using this method is developed by studying simulated data, theoretical background, calculation, per unit cost and its benefits in different aspects.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Vector controlled PMSM Drive modulated with Sinusoidal PWM and Space Vector PWM
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) are considered as energy efficient motors suitable for modern applications like electric vehicles. Field oriented control or vector control is a superior control strategy for PMSM drives. It is known that in vector control, decoupled control of torque and flux is obtained as in the case of a DC motor. The objective of this paper is to compare and analyze the performance of a vector controlled Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor which uses Sinusoidal PWM and space vector PWM techniques. Sinusoidal PWM and Space vector PWM are pulse width modulation techniques used for controlling the three phase inverter which drives the motor. They have the advantage of decreased harmonic content in the generated output voltage. Space vector modulation has the added advantage of increased DC bus utilization. Here both the methods are implemented along with FOC to control the PM motor and the results are analyzed. Simulation is carried out in MATLAB Simulink platform and the results are compared.

articleTitle: Prosumer Participation in a Transactive Energy Marketplace: A Game-Theoretic Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents a framework of transactive energy marketplace (TEM) in a community microgrid with multiple prosumers as market participants for facilitating peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading with demand response consideration. The internal market prices are determined using generation-to-demand ratio with the help of transactive energy market operator (TEMO). The TEMO is a non-profited retail energy manager that aims to enable prosumers to participate in the TEM, and to sustain equilibrium between community generation and demand. The participants in TEM are encouraged to trade their net demand with the neighborhood besides the upstream utility. The interactions between TEMO and prosumers are modeled with the game-theory. The optimal time slots for the schedulable loads of the prosumers in TEM are obtained using genetic algorithm while optimizing the energy bills. With the presented system, the reduction in the community energy bills is in the range of 18-52% in the P2P marketplace compared to conventional peer-to-grid (P2G) marketplace under different scenarios.

articleTitle: Case Study: Power Factor Improvement and Harmonic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: With increase in power supply demand and much new advancement in power system, the necessity to maintain the quality of power supply is increased. The paper presents a case study of SOMIKA CONGO, Copper Refining unit power system. The study is concluded to the selection of an appropriate capacitor bank for power factor correction. The result has been procured by ETAP (Electromagnetic Transient Analysis Program). ETAP Harmonic Analysis module involves modelling the frequency characteristics of different components of power systems, computing harmonic indices at given buses and branches, identifying problems associated with the existing harmonics, and providing an environment to simulate and test any mitigation methods.

articleTitle: A Novel Switching Scheme for Regenerative Braking and Battery Charging for BLDC motor Drive Used in Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: The development of a simple and cost effective driving system for electric vehicles (EVs) will improve their driving range. But to achieve this objective, the vehicle should be equipped with separate circuits for motor driving, regenerative braking and battery charging which increases the complexity. The paper discusses a novel scheme to reduce this complexity by introducing a switching pattern so as to accomplish these three modes of operation in a Brushless Direct Csurrent (BLDC) motor with the help of a single circuit itself. During motoring mode of operation, the converter acts as a three-phase inverter and for charging operation from the AC grid, the same three phase inverter acts as a rectifier which is connected to a buck converter by properly changing the switching pattern. Further, during regenerative braking mode, the same converter itself acts as a boost converter and feeds power back to the supply side. The simulation results presented in the paper prove the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Solar Window as an Energy Source : A Patent Study
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: A study on the evolution of solar panels/cells within a window has been carried out within the patent database. This paper is a review of the study on solar window. The retrieved patent records were analysed and categorized into different technologies depending on the technical aspect. Several trends in this technology are studied. A timeline of the solar window technology has been presented based on this study. Block diagrams of solar window have been presented before and after significant technical advancements. Several methods of increasing transparency and ventilation of a solar window are discussed. The paper also examines different optical elements used for concentrating light on the solar cells as part of the light concentration technology. This study helps researchers in the field to be aware of the technology trends and develop further as an alternative to the rooftop panels.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of BLDC Motor Drive using Vibration Spectrum Analysis: Part II
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper discusses the fault diagnosis of the Permanent Magnet (PM) Brushless DC (BLDC) motor drive using vibration signatures of the motor. Finite Element (FE) based co-simulation modelling of a PM BLDC motor is used for obtaining the vibration spectrum of the machine under healthy and fault conditions. The continuous operation of a PM BLDC motor in industrial applications steers to unfavorable environmental conditions leading to the emergence of faults. Faults can be of various types depending on the cause and effect in addition to the location of existence in the machine. However, in the proposed research work, the demagnetization fault in the rotor PMs is currently under study. Such faults on the rotor side is generally inflicted by the changes in magnetic coercivity (HC) leading to the demagnetization of a PM in the motor. A fault can be predicated in its incipient state by investigating the changes encountered in the vibration spectrum of the machine. Every individual component of the vibration spectrum is affected by the change in machine quantities, thus diagnosing the fault. Therefore, the characteristic performance of a BLDC motor is investigated through the numerical based co-simulation analysis for the diagnosis machine faults.

articleTitle: Modeling of Grid Connected PMSG based WECS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Nowadays, the use of wind energy for generating electricity is increasing and with the advancement of power electronic converters use of permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) is become popular as it has several advantages over other variable speed wind turbine generators. The main contribution of this research work is to develop a mathematical model of grid-connected PMSG based wind energy conversion system (WECS). The model is simulated using MATLAB SIMULINK (Simulink root library only). In this research work modeling of different components of WECS which includes wind turbine model, PMSG model, a functional model of ac to dc converter and voltage source inverter (VSI) is done. Converters are mathematically model using the switching functions.

articleTitle: A Novel Fault Tolerant Control Scheme for Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel switch fault-tolerant operation for switched-mode power conversion. The switch fault-tolerant scheme is implemented on the boost converter operates with a redundant switch. The redundant/secondary switch is driven by a delayed version of primary switching pulses. Both the switches provide charging paths to the inductor when individually turned-on. Thus, the inductor experiences doubled operating frequency than individual switches. Since the operating switching frequency is shared by two switches the control scheme allows the switches to share equal currents in healthy conditions. If one of the switches gets failed, the closed-loop control reconfigures the switching pulse width such that the healthy switch could provide the required power. The key features of the proposed schemes are low component count, continuous operation of the redundant switch, and less circuit complexity. For evidence of the proposed control scheme, MATLAB/Simulink results are presented. The simulation results of 600 W Boost Converter show promising operation in faulty conditions.

articleTitle: A Study on Exploration for Resource Utilization of Solar Energy on the Roof of APSRTC Buses
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: In highly colonized and emergent countries like India, the majority of the people are depending on public transportation like road and rail. In most of the places like semi-urban and rural areas where railways are not available, on-road transportation, particularly by buses, is being practiced. These buses will be moving or halting under the sun in almost all day hours and hence their roof exposes to sun irradiation during sunny hours. By placing appropriate solar collectors on the roof of buses, maximum solar energy can be extracted to the extent possible. The resourced solar energy can be converted into electricity, which then can be utilized in diversified ways. This paper presents results of a research study carried out on various types of buses belonging to one of the bus depots of APSRTC located at latitude 13.5706 N and longitude 79.4884 E. The study explored that, total 1336.713 kWh of electricity can be generated by installing appropriate size of the solar PV system on the vacant roof areas of six categories of total 150 buses belonging to the concern bus depot. The generated electricity is sufficient to charge, 746 numbers 12V 150AH deep cycle batteries daily and could pave a path for next-generation battery charging stations for driving electric vehicles. The contribution of this paper could become one of the lines of assault to reduce energy intensity through the transportation sector.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Integration of a Transformer-based Multi Level Inverter With Lesser Components
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents a transformer-based multilevel inverter (MLI) integrated with a photovoltaic system. It has lower number of components than a conventional MLI, thereby reducing the overall cost. Here, a nine level MLI is designed with only eight switches, whereas 16 switches are required for achieving a nine-level voltage in a conventional transformer-less MLI. The design has multiple H-bridges and a single transformer fed from a single dc source. The transformer helps in achieving the process of intermediate voltage regulation. A pulse width modulation (PWM) scheme is used to obtain the gate pulses. Another advantage of the design is that, only one dc source is used for the MLI. Also, several switching redundancies are possible for various voltage levels of the MLI. This decreases the switching losses. The photovoltaic integrated system is verified using MATLAB simulations and a basic hardware of the MLI is also made.

articleTitle: Super Twisting Algorithm Based Slip Ratio Control of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Safety of a passanger is an important feature that is considered much during the design of an electric vehicle (EV). A perfect traction control technique is essential to acheive this goal. Wheel slip ratio control method is widely accepted in stability control area of EV. Recently different sliding mode algorithms are used for the slip ratio control, among them super twisting control (STC) is proved to be one of the efficient method. For STC the estimation of wheel slip ratio is obtained by different nonlinear observers. In this work for the estimation of slip ratio from vehicle and wheel velocities a super twisting observer (STO) is proposed. Efficiency of the super twisting observer/controller system is validated in MATLAB/simulink model. A performance comparison is made with first order sliding mode observer/STC system. Results confirms the advancement of STO/STC system in speed of response, acccuracy and chattering reduction.

articleTitle: Implementation of Sensorless Vector Control PMSM Drive for Electrical Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper discusses the a Sensor-less control method of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) to be applied for its application to an Electric Vehicle. A Sensorless velocity and position control technique for a sliding mode observer(SMO) based PMSM. Implementation of the different control loop will be done in order to perform simulations that prove the correct operation of electric machine under this kind of control.

articleTitle: A Modified SEPIC Converter Based Solar Power Integration with Single Phase Utility Bus
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: In this paper, the performance of a modified DC-DC single-ended primary inductance converter (SEPIC) as the first stage of a grid integrated solar photovoltaic (PV) system is analysed. The incremental conductance (INC) based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm is used to control the high gain SEPIC converter while the inverter at the stage is synchronized to the grid by real time unit template monitoring. The chosen SEPIC topology provides high voltage gain at moderate duty ratios and removes the panel hotspot issues. The proposed system is designed and studied in MATLAB/Simulink platform under different test conditions. The performance of modified SEPIC converter and the overall grid tied system is found to be satisfactory under varying irradiation conditions and in terms of THD standards.

articleTitle: Non Inverting Buck-Boost Converter with PV fed BLDC Drive for Irrigation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: In this paper a non-inverting buck-boost DC-DC converter for pumping system used in irrigation and employing a PV fed Brushless DC Motor drive is proposed. This converter gives a positive polarity of output voltage compared to buck-boost and Cuk converter. Perturb & Observe algorithm is accomplished to increase the output of PV array. The output voltages from the converter are given to Voltage Source Inverter which drives the Brushless DC motor pump system. The proposed water pumping system performance for irrigation is compared with buck-boost converter and Cuk converter based system. Result shows less voltage stress and superior performance of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Vibration Analysis of Brushless Permanent Magnet Motor using Numerical Methods: Part I
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper discusses the Finite Element (FE) based co-simulation modelling of a Permanent Magnet (PM) Brushless DC (BLDC) motor for mechanical vibration analysis. The sources and causes of vibrations in the BLDC motor can be electromagnetic quivering, aerodynamic disturbances and mechanical oscillations. However, in this work the study on electromagnetic vibrations on BLDC motor performance has been done. The individual component of the vibrations is affected by the change in machine quantities under operation. Therefore, the characteristic performance of a Maxwell 2D and 3D model of a BLDC motor is investigated through the Ansys Workbench based co-simulation analysis. Under the operating conditions, the surface force densities, distribution of radial forces and electromagnetic solutions are obtained. The surface force density and force distribution are used for Modal and Harmonic-Response based analysis to monitor the health of the machine under operation. The electromagnetic solutions obtained in terms of magnitude, frequency and direction of vibrations, determine the state of health of a BLDC motor. The data thus, obtained can be used in future research work for the diagnosis of faults in the machine drive.

articleTitle: Xilinx System Generator-based Rapid Prototyping of Different Control Strategies for Solid State Transformer
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Solid-state transformer (SST) is a developing technology that is widely used in distribution systems for integrating renewable energy sources. Out of the numerous topologies available for SST, a Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter based SST is the most commonly utilized one due to its control efficiency. DABs are isolated bidirectional DC DC converters (IBDC) which has soft switching capabilities, high power density, bidirectional power flow, galvanic isolation, etc. When the SST is connected to the grid, it requires a monolithic platform for the fast controlling, reliable operation and protection enhancement of the converters of the SST. In this paper, Xilinx System Generator (XSG) platform is used for the rapid prototyping of the SST that directly generates the HDL code for the target control board. The different control strategies of DAB such as Single Phase Shift (SPS), Extended Phase Shift (EPS) and Dual Phase Shift (DPS) are studied and compared with XSG which is developed in MATLAB simulation platform. In this work, XSG based Hardware in the Loop (HIL) simulation of the three control strategies is done in XSG, and the results are verified.

articleTitle: Harmonic Mitigation in Induction-Motor Drives using Active Filtering Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a harmonic mitigation method in open ended induction-motor drive based on active filtering approach. Open ended motor has open stationary windings with two separate inverters feeding from either sides. With half input dc voltage this conventional configuration works as a three-level inverter. In this work, the stator winding is fed from one end by a SVPWM controlled primary voltage source inverter and other end by a secondary voltage source inverter. The secondary voltage source inverter is controlled to produce a voltage which will cancels out the harmonics in the motor phases. It is controlled using a series active filter algorithm to eliminate phase voltage harmonics, thereby reducing the motor losses and improves the efficiency and life span of the motor. The total harmonic distortion of the proposed drive scheme is less compared to conventional three-level open ended motor with additional advantage of no extra switching devices required. The proposed method is validated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of a New Five Level MLM based Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: In this paper, a novel cascaded multi-level inverter (MLI) with a multi-level module (MLM) is introduced. The inverter consists of sub multi-level units and a full bridge circuit. The added advantage of the novel topology is the reduction in components count as the level of output voltage raise. By increasing the number of output voltage levels the power quality can be improved. The harmonic content in the output voltage of the MLI can be minimized by applying a PWM optimization strategy. Here a multi carrier phase disposition (PD) PWM with constant frequency method is used to trigger the gate pulses. The novel topology has better performance and low THD when operating at desired voltage and power. The operation and performance of the multi-level module based 5 level MLI has been simulated in PSIM.

articleTitle: Modulated Model Predictive Current Control of a Three-Phase Photovoltaic Central Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: A three-phase two-level voltage source inverter is the most widely adopted configuration for the grid-integration of large-scale photovoltaic energy systems. To obtain high energy conversion during a wide dynamic range and to comply with the stringent grid codes, faster and high-performance nonlinear controllers are required. This paper develops a novel modulated model predictive current control method to control the photovoltaic central inverter for maximum energy yield and reactive power control. The developed control method estimates the future values of stationary-frame grid currents and assesses them by a duty-cycle optimized cost function. Three stationary voltage vectors corresponding to the low cost value are then synthesized by the space vector modulation stage to produce gating signals for the central inverter. The proposed control method ensures constant switching frequency, low steady-state errors and fast transient response simultaneously during rapid environmental changes. To verify the feasibility of the developed control method, simulation studies are conducted on a 1-MVA photovoltaic system, under solar irradiance, temperature and reactive power changes.

articleTitle: Investigation of High Voltage Circuit Breaker by Mathematical Modelling of Arc Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Circuit breaker is an essential component for power system protection. Mathematical models of arc help analyze arc behaviour by which interruption process of circuit breaker can be understood. This paper aims at investigating the current interruption process in circuit breaker by considering Mayr and Schwarz arc models. Effect on arc voltage and post arc current with the variation of cooling power and time constant parameters in Mayr arc model is described in this paper. Method to derive parameters of Schwarz arc model is presented in this paper. Comparison of Mayr arc model and Schwarz arc model is shown.

Author Keywords: Rate of Rise of Restrike Voltage (RRRV)

articleTitle: A New current control technique for minimization of sub and inter harmonics in 1-phase H-bridge Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: A current control technique for 1-phase H-bridge / Voltgae Source Inverter (VSI) is projected here. This current control is a modified hysteresis type. The advised hysteresis current control technique (HCCT) associates the profits of both bipolar and unipolar switching technique. This advised advanced HCCT reduces switching loss, eliminates the EMI effect by reducing the higher order harmonics and further more diminishes the Sub and Inter Harmonics (SIH) of the load current. Authors also compared results of the proposed control technique with some of existing HCCT. The simulation results, harmonic analysis of the load current of the novel control technique and other existing techniques are proposed and compared in the article.

articleTitle: Islanding detection technique for multi-port grid-integrated DC microgrid based on superimposed components
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: An islanding detection scheme is proposed for multi-port grid-integrated Photovoltaic (PV) based DC microgrid. DC Microgrid, the future distribution system, is used to interconnect distributed generation (DG) units and DC loads. Voltage source converter (VSC) with bidirectional power flow capability is used to connect the DC microgrid to the main grid for better utilization of generated power. One of important monitoring function of VSC control algorithm is the reliable detection of islanding. In this paper, detection of islanding condition is proposed by using a transient energy approach dealing with the analysis of the superimposed component of the Point of Common Coupling (PCC) voltage and VSC current. The islanding detection loop is further implemented with existing control algorithm of the VSC. In MATLAB, the system is designed using the Simulink. The results of the simulation obtained indicate the efficacy of the implemented scheme to differentiate between the islanding and non-islanding conditions.

articleTitle: Modeling of LLC converter Using Synchronous Reference Frame Transformation Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: The LLC (inductor-inductor-capacitor) converter is the widely used soft-switching resonant DC-DC converter. As a multi-resonant, variable-frequency converter, the LLC converter modeling is complex. Several methods have been proposed for modeling and controlling the LLC converter in literature. In this paper, the Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) based modeling approach is proposed which helps to derive a simplified model for switching frequency to output voltage transfer function in the case of LLC converter. The dominant circuit parasitic elements such as secondary side semiconductor switch drop, dc resistance (DCR) of resonant inductor and transformer, and equivalent series resistance (ESR) of output capacitor are incorporated into the SRF model. Inclusion of these parasitics results in an accurate LLC converter model. The derived model is used to design controller for Voltage Mode Control (VMC) of LLC converter. This controller is implemented using 16-bit Digital Signal Controller (DSC). The proposed model and digital controller are verified through experiments. The model prediction and experimental frequency response plots are found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: On-grid system evaluation for EV charging stations using renewable sources of energy
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: The Indian Automobile Industry is the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> largest in the world. India, in its effort to switch to electric vehicles and reduce its carbon emissions, launched the National Electric Mobility Mission Plan 2020 in 2013. It formulated the Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) scheme in 2015 to promote the manufacturing of electric and hybrid vehicle technology and to ensure sustainable growth of the same. However, the adoption rate was not satisfactory. One of the main reasons for the slow pace of adoption of electric vehicles by the customers was the lack of supporting charging infrastructure. In order to plan for charging stations, it is important to forecast the energy demand and design the system using renewable sources of energy. This paper proposes a renewable energy model for charging stations that can be implemented in the pilot city of New Delhi. A software tool, Hybrid Optimization of Multiple Energy Resources (HOMER) is used for the simulation and analysis.

articleTitle: Application of DPWM on 3D Space Vector Modulation with ghγ coordinate system for Three Phase Inverters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the three dimensional space vector modulation technique and its implementation using ghγ coordinate system for a three phase four wire inverters. The increased population of distributed generation and its resulting unbalances in the three-phase system demands 3D space vector modulation for the inverter switching. The new 3D coordinate system, ghγ is a non-orthogonal coordinate system, derived from the αβγ coordinate system for four wire inverters. Past researchers in this field developed a number of alternate coordinate methods to improve the system with primary focus to reduce computational complexity, common mode voltage as well as switching loss. This paper shows that the application of discontinuous PWM on three dimensional space vector modulation reduces switching loss and common mode voltage.

articleTitle: Electrical Energy Extraction from Unused Heat Energy of Hybrid EVs by Using Peltier Panel for Auxiliary Loads
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper gives the theoretical idea about energy recovery method from unused heat energy produced by internal combustion engine(IC engine) and electrical motors in hybrid electrical vehicles (HEV). This heat energy converts again into electrical energy to charge the separate battery source for auxiliary loads like headlights, indicators, air-conditioners, mobile adapters, and self-ignition of the electrical vehicle (EV). These loads consumes approximately 500watts of energy according to their utilization, this rating is around 5-15% of overall electrical vehicle's (EV) capacity. This paper describes about the conversion of unused heat energy into electric energy by using Peltier Panel for auxiliary load applications while hybrid electrical vehicle (HEV) is running. This method increases the efficiency of electric motors at the same time increases the kilometres per charge of electrical vehicle (EV).

articleTitle: One Day Ahead Indian Electricity Price Forecasting Using Intelligently Tuned SVR
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Power transaction process are competitive in restructured markets. Market operations such as bidding, hedging, planning of facility investments and negotiation of bilateral contracts are rely on electricity price. Electricity price uncertainty is the major barrier in profit maximization of market participants. This price uncertainty can be addressed by using accurate forecasts in market operations. Artificial intelligence and time series-based models are used for day ahead electricity price forecasting. Such models necessitate massive training inputs for accurate forecasting, which leads to high processing time. However, fast and accurate forecasts are required for real time decision making in market operations. Therefore, this paper proposes three support vector regression forecasting models for day ahead electricity price forecasting. Proposed models use limited quantum of training inputs as they use similar day approach for forecasting. Also, proposed model use GA and PSO based hyper parameter optimization for improving forecasting accuracy. Data collected from Indian power market is used for performance evaluation. Performance of proposed models are compared with linear regression and artificial neural network models. Results show that proposed models have very strong potential towards day ahead electricity price forecasting.

articleTitle: Advanced Health Assessment of Generator by Diagnostic Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Condition assessment is the core competence of diagnostician to safeguard the generator. This paper summarized the diagnostic reasoning in advanced health assessment of dielectric insulation system. State-of-art diagnostic test tools are briefed. Importance of machine knowledge in interpretation is outlined. Case studies are presented to highlight the valuable contribution of diagnosticians in assessing the health.

articleTitle: A Versatile Statcom for SSR Mitigation and Dynamic Reactive Power Management in DFIG Based Wind Farm Connected to Series Compensated Line
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Importance of wind energy incorporated power system is increasing day by day because of the economic benefits offered by it. However, the long distance transmission necessitates the use of series capacitors to compensate for the inductance of the AC transmission lines and to improve the transmission capacity of the system. Sub synchronous resonance (SSR) phenomenon is one of the major problem faced by the series compensated wind power systems. In this paper, a static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) with a SSR damping controller is proposed to mitigate SSR. Also a dynamic reactive power management system is implemented to produce the reactive power reference signals for STATCOM and DFIG. Reactive power reference signals are generated by making use of reactive power signals at the point of common coupling of wind power system and STATCOM. This helps in ensuring that the reactive power supply demanded by the line is met.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of Renewable Energy Resources in Microgrid Considering Stochastic Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: Optimal allocation and suitable sizing of Distributed Generation (DG) units have vital role in reducing power losses and improving voltage stability of power system. In this paper, considering voltage stability improvement and power losses reduction as objectives, the evaluation of siting and sizing of DG units including stochastic nature of DG has been investigated. To achieve these, power loss and voltage stability are taken as the objective functions considering different operating constraints and the probabilistic nature of DG, modelled using probability density function. Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) is applied to solve the multi-objective problem. The solution method has been tested on IEEE-33 bus standard radial distribution systems. The ability of the proposed method in enhancing of voltage stability, and reduction of power losses are confirmed using simulation results.

articleTitle: Effective Saliency Based Initial Rotor Position Estimation of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for High torque applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper proposes an effective method for the initial rotor position estimation of interior PMSM. The smooth start-up of a PMSM drives heavily relies on the accurate initial rotor position. Improper initial rotor position value leads to starting failure or temporary reverse rotation. This method utilizes the line to line inductance values to estimate the rotor position. High-frequency voltage signals injection and the rotating coordinate transformation technique used to extract rotor position information from the inductance values. The pole identification is done by using the current saturation concept and SVPWM switching sequence. This method effectively helps to avoid temporary reverse rotation and starting failures. The validity and practical applications of the proposed estimation technique are verified through the experimental outcomes. The proposed method has been implemented on a microcontroller (TMS320F28035). The obtained experimental results confirm the effectiveness of these methods.

articleTitle: Computation based Comparison of LVDC with AC for Off-Grid Energy Efficient Residential Building
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: It is a fact that the renewable energy sources (RES) such as Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) and fuel cells are inherently DC power sources. The importance of the switch to cleaner and renewable source of energy that is generated "as local as possible" need to be acknowledged. However, a historically established distribution system that is AC based is prevailing. This requires DC-AC converters for the integration of solar energy to the existing power distribution infrastructure. Increasing usage of DC powered equipment and the introduction of electric vehicle charging stations in the power system will add to the further increase in consumption of DC Power. Due to the difference in the modes of power generated and consumed, clean and renewable DC power generated need to be converted to AC power for supply and distribution compatibility and later again forced to re-convert major part of the incoming AC power to DC power for end use for residential applications. This conversion and reconversion, results in adding losses and increasing complexity to the system. The DC-AC-DC conversions are reduced to a certain extent by introducing a Low Voltage DC (LVDC) system. This report investigates the potential for using LVDC system in residences with on-site solar PV power generation by calculating the net power drawn by a direct-DC powered house compared to a similar house with AC distribution, considering identical DC-internal loads. Also the number of PV panels required for supplying the load and the storage batteries is calculated for both AC and 48V LVDC system. It is clearly seen that over and above the savings in energy, there is an added advantage of huge savings on initial investments, which may unlock the resistance and give an extra mileage when performing the payback calculations for these upgrades.

articleTitle: Design of a Full-Bridge Converter for Lead-Acid Battery Charging and Powering DC Loads
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Power and Renewable Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents a design procedure for a hard switched full-bridge ac-dc converter for constant voltage / current controlled charging of Lead-Acid Batteries. The converter is designed to operate in two-stage charging control or Constant Current Constant Voltage (CC/CV). The converter also acts as a regulated dc power supply for dc loads connected in parallel with the battery at the secondary side of the converter. Initially, the battery charges with the constant current set manually, as and when the battery terminal voltage reaches a threshold value corresponding to the battery's full voltage, the control method changes to constant voltage mode to keep the battery voltage constant near its float voltage. Step by step method for converter design is illustrated along with the load v/s efficiency comparison for various switching frequency designs. The results show that losses at partial loading are higher when the operating frequency increases; to overcome this, low-medium switching frequency and lower saturation flux density in the magnetics can be chosen, but at the expense of larger sized transformer and inductor in the circuit. Finally, the converter design is simulated in MATLAB Simulink to verify the output as per the specification.
